ticket.title: Paid domains showing Unpaid and cancelled after workspace move; $90 recovery payment didn’t restore inboxes
ticket.description:
#### Customer Name

Name 14

#### Customer Email

<email>

#### Workspace name

Company Six

#### Screenshot

#### What are you trying to achieve?

Get Company Six’s domains and inboxes restored and sending again, and get the domains moved from another workspace recognized as paid.

#### What are you doing to achieve it?

On October 15, the client paid $90 (Inbox DFY) to recover his domains and emails. He also moved his third client’s domains (<domain>, <domain>, <domain>, <domain> and <domain>) into this workspace to keep them active. His card has been paying successfully throughout: invoices show $90 on September 18, $18 on September 25, $185 on September 29, $90 on October 15 and $18 on October 16, all paid.

#### What is happening instead?

Company Six’s own domains and inboxes disappeared and stopped sending. The popup says 15 mailboxes on 5 domains were cancelled on October 5 for non payment, and it also says they’ll be cancelled on October 23. The $90 recovery payment didn’t bring them back. Five of the six domains now listed show Unpaid, even though their inboxes were paid on September 18 and 25. Only <domain> shows Paid.

#### What is the expected outcome?

Restore Company Six’s domains and inboxes, apply the existing payments to the moved domains so they show Paid, and confirm whether the October 15 $90 is applied or should be refunded.

relatedSnapshot.title: Pre-warmed paid state is written only by a client confirmation call and the reconcile lane ignores orders under an hour: a captured payment can leave the workspace unprovisioned in pending_payment
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

A pre-warmed domain/inbox order's paid state is written only by a client-side confirmation call; there is no provider-side signal for Autumn-billed pre-warmed checkouts. When that call does not complete, the customer's money is captured, the domain and inbox entitlements sit live and unused in billing, and the workspace keeps showing the order as "waiting for payment" with nothing provisioned and no way for anyone to move it.

## Problem

The customer pays, sees an empty mailbox list, and is told the order is still waiting for payment. Nothing in the product or in an admin tool can confirm or provision it. The only recovery is a scheduled pass that cannot select an order younger than an hour, and its newest-order-per-account gate can push a paid order out of that lane entirely. If no pass reaches the order within 24 hours the stale-order cron cancels it, so the customer waits up to a day for items they have already paid for.

## Root cause

A pre-warmed order's paid state is written in exactly two places, and this defect bypasses both:

* `apps/web/trpc/routers/billing.ts` `confirmDomainPurchase` (line 2541), reached only from client code: `apps/web/components/campaigns/email-accounts/buy-all/checkout-view.tsx` (`proceedWithCheckout` -> `handlePaymentSuccess`, the leg used when `createMultiAttachCheckout` returns no payment URL under `redirect_mode: 'if_required'`), `apps/web/components/campaigns/email-accounts/checkout-return-handler.tsx` (`handleCheckoutReturn`), and `apps/web/components/campaigns/email-accounts/domain-provisioning-status.tsx` (`handleCompletePayment` on the pending-order card).
* `apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/billing/reconcile-domain-orders-cron.ts`, step `find-pending-orders-to-check`, which selects pending_payment orders only with `lt(createdAt, oneHourAgo)` and only for the newest actionable order per organization and billing account (`find-latest-actionable-orders-per-billing-account`).

No file under `apps/web/app/api/webhooks` writes a domain purchase order for Autumn-billed orders; `apps/web/app/api/webhooks/autumn/route.ts` handles products-updated and lapse events only, and the Whop partner webhook is the only provider-side writer, covering partner organizations. Verified at commit 4845e5940e1eb56662b687e98f54ed92a1de45de.

## Blast radius

Confirmed affected: 1 workspace, 1 user — one captured charge, 9 domains and 27 inboxes provisioned = 0, with the entitlements live and unused in billing. Counted 2026-09-24.

Potentially exposed, counted 2026-09-24: a production-side proxy for orders whose client confirmation did not land is a paid pre-warmed Autumn order whose `paid_at` falls within 10 minutes after `last_payment_check_at` (the reconcile pass confirmed it, not the client leg) — 76 of 843 paid pre-warmed Autumn orders created in the previous 90 days, including repeat orders from the affected workspace, counted with `select count(*) filter (where paid_at is not null and last_payment_check_at is not null and paid_at >= last_payment_check_at and paid_at <= last_payment_check_at + interval '10 minutes') from domain_purchase_order where order_type='pre_warmed' and billing_account_id is not null and created_at > now() - interval '90 days'`. The proxy over-counts (a cron-checked paid order may also have been client-confirmed earlier) and cannot be split into "would have provisioned anyway" versus "saved only by the cron" without per-order provider reads, so exposure sits at or below 76.

Separately, pending_payment pre-warmed Autumn orders created in the last 7 days: 1 order / 1 organization, none older than an hour at count time; 2 pre-warmed orders were refunded by the reservation-expired lane in the same window.

## Proposed fix

A captured payment must end in a written paid state and provisioning, or in a refund, without depending on a client response: record the paid state from a provider-side signal for Autumn-billed pre-warmed orders, and close the blind window so an unpaid-looking order that has been paid is detected in minutes rather than after the hourly gate. Keep the newest-order-per-account gate from hiding an older paid order, and surface a state that separates "paid but not yet confirmed" from "abandoned", so support can act instead of guessing.

## What's included

In scope: the paid-state write path for pre-warmed Autumn orders, its provider-side signal, and the pending-payment selection window and ordering gate in the reconcile pass. Not in scope: the Whop partner path (it already records paid orders from its own webhook), the reservation-cancelled reactivation lane owned by ENG-14199, and the mail provider pipeline, which is never reached for these orders.

Worth owning separately, per the incident assessment for the triggering report:

* Customer recovery: provision an affected paid order or refund it when its reservations have lapsed — a human decision per workspace.
* Observability: no signal today distinguishes a paid-but-unconfirmed order from an abandoned one; the affected order was invisible until a customer reported it.
* Containment: the customer-facing "Complete payment" control on the pending-order card re-runs the checkout against already-attached subscriptions; its double-charge safety is unassessed, so it should not be advised until Autumn idempotency is confirmed.

## Regression seam

Boundary: the pending-payment confirmation of an Autumn-billed pre-warmed order. Trigger: a checkout whose subscription attach succeeds and settles payment while the client confirmation call never returns a paid state. Observable red before the fix: the order stays pending_payment with `paid_at` NULL and `last_payment_check_at` NULL, zero provisioned items, and no lane selecting it for at least an hour. Green after: the paid state is recorded from a server-side signal within minutes and provisioning starts, or the order is refunded with its reservations released.

## Done when

* A pre-warmed Autumn checkout whose payment is captured but whose client confirmation does not land is confirmed and provisioned, or refunded, without waiting for a customer report.
* A paid order cannot be excluded from recovery because it is less than an hour old or because a newer order exists on the same account.
* A regression test proves the causal mechanism at the pending-payment confirmation seam named above.
* The exposed population is re-counted after deployment and reported.

## Reports

* ENG-14226

relatedSnapshot.title: Clear stale purchase orders and unpaid warnings after a domain is cleaned up
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Problem

After a domain's billing has stopped and its inboxes are gone, its failed or abandoned purchase records can still show in Acquisity Billing with an unpaid or resubscribe warning. Customers see a payment problem for mailboxes they no longer have.

## What's included

* When the cleanup from ENG-14902 finishes for a domain, close out the `domain_purchase_order` rows that only covered cleaned-up domains (failed, abandoned or still pending payment), so they stop counting as unpaid.
* Resolve the domain's CMR unpaid finding and stop any further unpaid reminders for it.
* Billing and Email Accounts show the domain as removed, with the reason, instead of an unpaid badge, the pay-unpaid dialog or the resubscribe banner.
* Orders that still cover live domains are left alone.

## Done when

- [ ] A workspace whose domains were all cleaned up shows no unpaid badge, pay-unpaid prompt or resubscribe banner.
- [ ] A workspace with a mix of cleaned-up and live domains only loses the warnings for the cleaned-up ones.
- [ ] No further unpaid reminder emails go out for cleaned-up domains.
- [ ] Tests cover the order close-out, mixed orders and the UI states.

relatedSnapshot.title: Charged twice for the same domain and inbox bundle; one bundle was never delivered and its subscription is still billing
relatedSnapshot.description:
Intercom conversation: <url:app.intercom.com>

Conversation context: customer-initiated Intercom conversation, opened 2026-09-30, contact Name 7 <email>, workspace "Name 8 Workspace", owner role. Initial message: "I have a billing issue that isn't being sorted. Please escalate to someone asap!" Asked for detail: "I've been billed twice for emails and domains for the last 3 months when that's not what I'm using." Declined the self-serve answer: "No, I still need help." No attachments.

Bucket: overcharged.

Finding: the customer bought the same DFY bundle (1 domain + 3 inboxes) twice about 17 hours apart and was charged for both; only one bundle was ever delivered. Order <uuid> (domain <domain>, created 2026-07-23 14:01Z) was cancelled for "Payment timeout - order automatically cancelled after 30 minutes" with nothing provisioned, but its Autumn subscription and its Stripe charges landed anyway. Order <uuid> (domain <domain>, created 2026-07-24 06:47Z) completed and is the bundle the customer actually uses (3 active connected inboxes). The cancelled order's subscription was never cancelled, so it has kept invoicing every month since.

Exposure (Stripe, smallest currency unit, all succeeded and unrefunded, no credit notes):

* 2026-07-23, 3276 cents ($32.76), charge <stripe-id>, invoice EKGUJ5YE-0017
* 2026-08-23, 1800 cents ($18.00), charge <stripe-id>, invoice EKGUJ5YE-0021
* 2026-09-23, 1800 cents ($18.00), charge <stripe-id>, invoice EKGUJ5YE-0025
  Total already collected for the undelivered bundle: $68.76, and $18.00/month continues until the orphan subscription is cancelled. The delivered bundle's own charges are legitimate and are not part of this ask.

Proposed human action (proposal, not a promise): refund the $68.76 collected for the undelivered bundle, and cancel the orphan domain and inbox line items on the billing account so the recurring $18.00/month stops. A Stripe customer credit is the alternative if the customer would rather have it applied forward (the Legacy Pro plan bills monthly, so there is a future invoice to consume it). The customer has not yet said which they want. No money has been moved and nothing has been cancelled.

Full readout, systems of record, and the code path are in the Billing investigation document on this ticket.

relatedSnapshot.description:
## Customer report

```text
Customer attempted to reset onboarding for their workspace and instead deleted the entire workspace, losing purchased domains and campaigns. Workspace was on a legacy $1/month plan; customer reports being newly charged.

Billing summary shows on 2026-10-07: a $1 "Subscription update" charge (<stripe-id>) and a $42 "Subscription creation" charge (<stripe-id>) covering 1 domain ($18/yr) and 3 inboxes ($8/mo each). Both succeeded, neither refunded. The active subscription record still shows plan "Legacy" at $1/month, active.

A system reconciliation flag on this billing account states: "Stripe shows a succeeded charge, but the product database has no active subscription status. Check whether this organization was charged without being provisioned" — unresolved mismatch worth billing review.

Provisioning records show the 2026-10-07 order (domain + 3 inboxes) completed with 1 domain and 3 inboxes active, matching the charge. No tool here can confirm or rule out that the customer's workspace reset/deletion action caused these new charges, nor whether previously purchased domains/campaigns from before the reset are recoverable.

Customer's ask: refund of the new charges, since they believed the workspace was a static $1/month legacy plan and did not intend to purchase new domains/inboxes or lose existing campaigns. Flagging to billing team to review the charges, the reconciliation mismatch, and whether a refund is appropriate.
```

relatedSnapshot.title: When payment gives up, stop the plan, mailboxes and domains cleanly
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

ENG-8112 documented the original seven-day warning and auto-cancel decision. The operating model was revised on 11 September 2026 after measuring how billing actually works. Inboxes are charged monthly on each subscription's own anniversary and domains yearly, so there is no advance invoice 28 or 14 days before renewal. When a payment fails we warn the customer, let the provider's retries run, then switch provider renewal off so the inboxes expire at the end of the month we have already paid for, leaving a free reactivation window. This ticket owns production enforcement across payment events, base-plan/workspace termination, Zapmail, Company Three, local state, recovery and audit evidence.

**Scope narrowed 29 Sep 2026.** This ticket now owns Flow B (the plan ends because the customer did not pay), Flow C (a mailbox payment fails while the plan is fine), the reactivation window and the provider-neutral design. Three parts moved out:

* the cancel steps themselves (renewal off at the supplier, per-domain resumable billing cancel) now live in ENG-14252;
* workspace and account deletion now lives in ENG-10782;
* the Autumn event classifier, the failure reason and the day 0, 3 and 7 warnings now live in ENG-13746.

Added: on Autumn, an expired plan never pauses campaigns today, because Autumn workspaces are always treated as protected. Autumn plans that expire must run the same pause and cleanup as Whop, and the automation switch (`SUBSCRIPTION_ACCESS_AUTOMATION_ENABLED`) is turned on after a dry-run review. Whether Acquisity/Acquisity#6288 is finished here or closed is an open question; recommended: close it and reuse the parts this ticket needs.

**Decided 29 Sep 2026:** no immediate cut-off. When billing stops (day 14, Stripe's final retry), supplier renewal is switched off and the mailboxes keep working until the month we have already paid the supplier for ends, then they are removed. We never cancel at the supplier early. The full timeline is on ENG-13358.

## Problem in plain English

When a mailbox payment fails, a base workspace plan is cancelled, or a workspace is deleted, customer access and Zapmail supplier billing can drift apart. Acquisity may stop collecting mailbox revenue while the Zapmail domain subscription remains live and billable.

A deletion can also remove the local records needed to find the supplier subscription later. One failed step can leave the mailbox active in Zapmail, connected in Company Three, hidden locally, or some combination of those states.

## Confirmed production gap

The production Autumn webhook transport is configured and receiving signed events, but the current handler only acts on new, renew, upgrade and downgrade base-plan transitions. It accepts `past_due`, `expired` and `cancel` events with HTTP 200, marks them processed and performs no mailbox cancellation or reconciliation. Since 11 August, 947 `past_due` events for domain or inbox products across 113 billing accounts reached this path without triggering supplier cleanup.

This ticket must change that behavior. Relevant events must be classified and durably enqueued. They must not be acknowledged as successfully processed when the required state transition was skipped.

## Detailed behavior

### How renewal timing actually works (measured 11 September 2026)

* Each inbox subscription renews monthly on its own anniversary. The provider charges us about a day before it, and the customer's Autumn anniversary is effectively the same moment (median gap under an hour across a 1,800 domain sample).
* So a failed customer payment has always already cost us one provider month. Accept that month rather than moving billing anchors.
* About 12% of pre-warmed domains were registered as provider stock before a customer bought them, so their provider dates differ from the customer's. Every cutoff must use the provider period end, never the customer billing date.
* Domains are yearly and renew separately. Domain renewal is owned by ENG-13745.

### What cancel means (the same steps for every reason)

1. **Stop charging.** For a customer's own cancellation, stop at the end of the period they have paid for. For non-payment, stop immediately with no further retries.
2. **Switch provider renewal off for the inbox subscription.** The inboxes keep working until the end of the month already paid for, then expire. Never cancel immediately while a paid month is running.
3. **Reactivation window.** Until that provider month ends, a customer who pays or resubscribes gets everything back: renewal back on, billing re-attached, inboxes still warm.
4. **At the end of the provider month,** once the provider confirms the inboxes expired: remove them from sending (where sending is a separate provider), mark the domain and inboxes cancelled, email the customer, and switch domain renewal off so the domain is not renewed.
5. **Campaigns pause when the plan ends,** not when the inboxes expire. This is ENG-10751 behaviour extended to Autumn.

### Flow B: the plan ends because the customer did not pay

Day 0 is the failed payment.

* Days 0 to about 14: the warnings in ENG-13746 while Autumn retries the card.
* About day 14: the plan expires. Plan, inboxes and domains all cancel using the steps above and campaigns pause. Email: "Your plan has ended. Your inboxes will be removed on {provider month end} unless you reactivate."
* 3 days before removal: "Last chance to keep your inboxes."
* At removal: "Your inboxes and domains were removed."
* Payment recovered at any point before removal: everything is restored and the customer gets "Payment received, you're all set."

### Flow C: an inbox payment fails while the plan is fine

* The same as Flow B but scoped to that domain's inboxes.
* Day 0: alert and email, "Payment failed for 12 inboxes on <domain>", with the failure reason and how to fix it. Reminders on day 3 and day 7, and a final warning 2 days before the stop date, each repeating the reason (decided 29 Sep 2026).
* At Autumn expiry: stop billing and switch provider renewal off. Take those inboxes out of active campaigns so campaigns keep sending from the rest.
* Reactivation window until the provider month ends, then removal and an email.

### Works with any inbox provider

We plan to move inboxes to Company Three. The timeline, reactivation window, emails and campaign pause live on our side, keyed to a generic provider period end. Each provider adapter supplies: read an inbox subscription's period end and renewal state; switch renewal on or off; renew or restore; confirm the inboxes ended; remove them from sending; list all inventory for the daily check. Where the provider and the sending platform are the same company, the remove-from-sending step is a no-op. Confirm how Company Three bills us before writing that adapter.

### Also fix

A customer cancelling a single domain goes through the same steps, ending at the end of the paid period on both sides. Today the provider is cancelled immediately while Autumn bills to period end, so the customer loses service they have paid for.

### Durable renewal and cancellation workflow

Use an explicit resumable paid lifecycle:

`notice_scheduled → customer_charge_due → paid_for_next_period → supplier_renewal_due → supplier_renewal_verified → occurrence_completed → next_occurrence_scheduled`

After failed collection:

`cure_window → supplier_nonrenewal_requested → supplier_nonrenewal_verified → supplier_period_ended → full_domain_deletion_requested → full_domain_deleted → downstream_cleanup_pending → billing_reconciled → completed`

Each transition records attempts, timestamp, idempotency key, provider response summary and last error. A retry resumes at the first incomplete transition and cannot repeat completed external actions.

For a managed inbox domain, an inbox subscription still unpaid at the safe cutoff schedules supplier non-renewal while preserving the already-paid mailbox period. Only after that period ends and conclusive provider readback confirms service ended may Acquisity delete the full associated domain and every included inbox. Customer notices must explicitly explain this whole-domain consequence.

Terminal Zapmail deletion uses Cold Mail Reseller `DELETE /domains`, which deprovisions the domain, DNS, mailboxes and associated subscriptions. Provider contract correction, verified 9 September 2026: the CMR subscription event contract says the cancel endpoint takes effect immediately and deactivates mailbox accounts. It must not be treated as end-of-cycle nonrenewal or dispatched early while promising the funded period remains available. Disabling subscription auto-renew is a separate, documented operation (`POST /subscriptions/toggle-autorenewal`). Per the provider's documented lifecycle, renewal off means the subscription goes past due at period end, gets a 7 day grace period, then expires and the mailboxes are deactivated. Verify this once in the provider sandbox, including that the paid month keeps running and that switching renewal back on restores the mailboxes, before wiring the production flow. An accepted cancellation request is not proof of full-domain cleanup.

Before completing cancellation, calculate any remaining customer-funded annual-domain value and record the explicitly approved refund, credit or no-refund outcome on the renewal occurrence. Existing historical waste handled by ENG-13362 may still require immediate full-domain deletion after fresh evidence and explicit approval.

Supplier deletion is confirmed only by the required response and conclusive domain/subscription readback. Company Three and local cleanup run only after the current supplier period ended and readback confirms service ended or the domain was deleted. A future non-renewal alone is not cleanup authorization. Downstream failures remain independently retryable and cannot restart supplier service, block cost prevention or repeat a destructive action.

### Workspace and account deletion

* Workspace, billing-account, order and mailbox deletion must not cascade away supplier identity or cancellation evidence.
* Trigger the same deprovisioning workflow before destructive deletion, or retain a tombstone until cleanup is complete.
* If safety requires blocking deletion until supplier cleanup succeeds, return a clear operator/customer error.
* Cover self-service, admin, bulk, script and framework deletion entry points that can affect the scoped inventory.

### Recovery, reversals and billing access

* Payment recovery before supplier non-renewal returns the occurrence to `paid_for_next_period`.
* Recovery after non-renewal was requested requires authoritative provider reconciliation. If cancellation cannot be reversed, either provision a new explicitly approved resource or refund/credit the customer; never claim the old resource was restored.
* Recovery after provider deletion requires new checkout or approved comp and never silently recreates infrastructure.
* A refund, dispute, chargeback or credit reversal before the supplier cutoff makes the future period uncovered and enters the cure/non-renewal path.
* If money is reversed after Acquisity paid the supplier, preserve live service for the funded supplier period, flag the contradiction, prevent the next renewal and apply the approved debt/refund/access policy.
* If the customer cancels after advance collection, refund only when supplier renewal can still be safely prevented. Otherwise preserve service for the funded period and schedule the following renewal off.
* If the customer paid but supplier renewal fails, enter supplier recovery and preserve entitlement plus Company Three/local linkage. Complete only after readback proves restored service, or apply the defined refund/credit outcome if it cannot be restored.
* Ending the base workspace plan does not itself prove a separately paid or approved-free inbox subscription is unpaid. Evaluate each managed inbox domain against its own inbox entitlement and supplier period.
* Customers without an active base plan retain a billing-only route to view affected resources, warning, amount, payment recovery and cancellation deadline.

## Suggested implementation route

* Extend the signed Autumn event path and scheduled renewal backstop around the same durable renewal occurrence. Name 12 advance payment failure and recovery quickly; scheduled jobs own the reminder steps, the cutoff at the provider period end and the final provider readback. Provider calls stay outside the webhook request.
* Keep provider calls out of the webhook request. Persist the event idempotently, enqueue the durable workflow, and return success only after the required transition has been recorded.
* Route delinquency deadlines, base-plan termination and workspace deletion through one shared cancellation orchestrator.
* Build the state machine on durable records introduced by the entitlement ticket.
* Derive idempotency from the immutable entitlement plus cancellation occurrence, not from a domain name or scheduler run.
* Reuse the existing Cold Mail Reseller cancellation audit foundation where it satisfies these guarantees.
* Add operational alerts and an admin view for incomplete or repeatedly failing transitions.

## Done when

* the existing Autumn webhook no longer acknowledges and discards relevant `past_due`, `expired` or `cancel` events;
* tests prove the exact event scenarios above enqueue one idempotent transition and irrelevant products remain ignored;
* every cutoff is derived from the provider period end, and duplicate events cannot reset a deadline or the notification history;
* duplicate events cannot reset grace or duplicate cancellation;
* payment recovery before supplier cancellation stops pending removal;
* supplier, Company Three, local and billing steps are resumable and individually auditable;
* base-plan cancellation and every workspace deletion path trigger the same guarantees;
* deletion cannot erase the evidence needed to finish cleanup;
* full-domain supplier deletion is verified against the exact domain, supplier subscription and included mailbox quantity;
* `/subscriptions/cancel` cannot be mistaken for completed full-domain offboarding;
* active campaigns are recorded and paused before Company Three removal, while Company Three or local failure cannot block or repeat confirmed Zapmail deletion;
* incomplete workflows alert with the failed transition, age and estimated monthly supplier cost;
* integration tests cover payment recovery before and after supplier cancellation, duplicate events, partial provider failure, workspace deletion with active mailboxes and retry from every transition.
* customer notices identify the full affected domain/inboxes, amount, charge date, cutoff and whole-domain deletion consequence;
* provider non-renewal preserves the already-paid period and never authorizes early Company Three/local disconnection;
* an unpaid managed inbox-domain subscription can delete the full domain only after period-end readback and deterministic annual-domain refund/credit/no-refund handling;
* deadlines are derived from authoritative supplier timestamps and stored in UTC; missing or drifting dates become operator exceptions;
* changed quantity, price or renewal timestamp invalidates the stale occurrence before collection;
* paid customer/supplier renewal failure enters recovery and ends only in verified restored service or deterministic refund/credit;
* tests cover payment recovery racing the cutoff, duplicate scheduler/webhook delivery, provider timeout after non-renewal, and two workers claiming the same occurrence;
* the base-plan cascade runs: plan expiry cancels inboxes and domains through the same steps, and campaigns pause at plan expiry;
* Flow C removes only the unpaid domain's inboxes while other campaigns keep sending;
* paying inside the reactivation window restores everything with no new setup or provisioning;
* no provider inbox stays live with renewal on for a customer who is not paying, checked by the daily read.

## Blocked by

* ENG-14252, for the shared cancel steps.
* ENG-13746, for the event classifier and warnings.

Do not run this at the same time as ENG-11454: both add a "stop at plan end" step, and whichever lands second reuses the first.

## Implementation context

AI context.md

### Existing-inbox management implementation slice (9 September 2026)

After ENG-13526, James confirmed that Acquisity/Acquisity#6288 must provide one owner/admin link to see all existing inbox groups, including active paid, free and credit-funded groups, with actual customer prices and current service periods. Clients can keep all, cancel all, or keep some whole domain groups and cancel others. Choices and their consequences must be reviewed before confirmation.

Keeping a group must recover any exact existing invoice without duplicating it, repair future payment collection where needed, and establish or restore recurring billing for retained inboxes without purchasing or provisioning new ones. Paying an invoice alone is not completion. Show invoice liabilities separately from future monthly charges. Preserve paid siblings, allocate shared coverage once, and keep annual domain/platform rights separate. Cancellation must record and verify exact billing and supplier effects, preserve funded periods, and show requested, scheduled, pending and completed states honestly. Promises, internal budgets and reversals require their recorded decisions before any automatic demand.

This scope supersedes the earlier invoice-only and selection-only implementation limitation. It retains this ticket's existing ownership and broader lifecycle contract, and reuses ENG-13359 entitlement and ENG-13361 reconciliation work. Unsupported or ambiguous provider actions must have a specific guided resolution and must not be reported as completed.

Implementation, tests and the draft PR are authorized, including a dedicated access-protected preview using a separate synthetic database and Autumn/Stripe test credentials. Production issuance, notices, real charges/refunds, production subscription changes, supplier cancellations, rollout and merge are not authorized. Outreach sending remains dependent on a verified working flow. This slice does not mark the lifecycle programme or estate cleanup complete.

## Intercom conversation

<url:app.intercom.com>

## Conversation context

Same Intercom thread as ENG-14509. On 2026-10-05 the customer (owner of the Company Four workspace) wrote: "The profile says review billing, and when we go in everything is in order, how do we resume the campaign?" Support answered that the campaign was active and not paused, then said "It seems that your payment for the inboxes did not go through. Kindly revisit your payment." Asked to check the Company Four workspace specifically, the customer replied "The payment date is only the 10th?" and, after support confirmed, asked: "Then how would the inbox payment not have gone through?"

## Testable claim

In the Company Four workspace, the 3 mailboxes on <domain> are flagged unpaid with a 6 October cancellation date, but the billing page lists no managed domains for that workspace, so the owner has no resubscribe control to pay for them and cannot act on the notice.

## Evidence

* Production audit row for the workspace: domain <domain>, payment_state 'unpaid' and open (no resolved_at, no dismissed_at) since 2026-09-10, held_domains 1, held_inboxes 3, paid_domains 0, paid_inboxes 0, mail_domain_status 'failed', note "Inboxes unpaid (aggregate)".
* The same row's order_id is a DFY domain purchase order whose status is 'refunded' (refunded 2026-08-11 after the provider failed to provision it; refundableDomains 1, refundableInboxes 3, retriesExhausted true).
* The workspace's only mail_domain row is that domain, status 'failed'. The provider-side mailbox subscription is still ACTIVE with auto-renew and period end 2026-10-11, and the 3 mailboxes exist and are 'active' in the app, so the workspace keeps sending from them.
* listManagedDomains filters out mail domains whose purchase order status is 'refunded' (and whose domain status is 'suspended'), so the managed list for this workspace is empty. EmailAccountsDomainsCard returns its "No managed domains" empty state before rendering the "Review and resubscribe" and per-domain "Resubscribe" controls, which are the only entry points to the pay-unpaid-mailboxes flow. The customer is an owner of the workspace, so the pay flow itself is available to her; it is simply unreachable from the page.
* Blast radius counted 2026-10-05: 4 organizations and 9 open 'unpaid' findings whose purchase order is refunded (query joined cmr_domain_audit_finding to domain_purchase_order on order_id, filtered payment_state 'unpaid', resolved_at and dismissed_at null, order status 'refunded').
* Two reminder emails for the unpaid mailboxes were sent on 2026-09-29 to <email> and <email>, which puts the notice's cancellation date at 2026-10-06 (7-day grace).
* The customer's report matches the code path: the billing page shows her nothing to pay.

## Code

* apps/web/trpc/routers/outreach/email-accounts.ts, listManagedDomains (the ne(domainPurchaseOrderTable.status, 'refunded') filter).
* apps/web/components/billing/email-accounts-domains-card.tsx, EmailAccountsDomainsCard (empty-state early return hides the resubscribe controls).

relatedSnapshot.title: Pre-warmed orders cancelled through the checkout (reservation timer or manual cancel) escape the cancelled-order payment reactivation lane: paid orders are never provisioned or refunded
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

A pre-warmed domain/inbox checkout that the reservation clock cancels while the customer is still inside the payment flow is never recovered, even when the payment then succeeds. The customer is charged, receives no domains and no inboxes, and nothing on any lane ever moves the order.

## Problem

The customer buys pre-warmed inboxes, submits payment, and sees an empty workspace: no domains, no email accounts, no provisioning card, and no way to cancel, retry, or refund from the product. The campaign that needed those inboxes cannot launch. Money has been captured at the provider.

## Root cause

The cancellation and the recovery disagree about what a cancelled order looks like.

* `apps/web/components/campaigns/email-accounts/buy-all/checkout-view.tsx` (reservation countdown effect) calls `cancelDomainReservation` when the timer reaches zero and that browser session has not initiated checkout; the manual Back button in the same view calls the identical mutation and writes the identical error string, so every cancellation through this path is affected, not only the timer's. The server-side mutation `cancelDomainReservation` in `apps/web/trpc/routers/outreach/email-accounts.ts` writes `status='cancelled'` and `error='User cancelled the reservation'`, releases the `domain_reservation` rows, and never writes `completed_at`, so it stays NULL.
* Recovery lane 1, `apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/billing/reconcile-domain-orders-cron.ts`. Its `find-latest-recently-cancelled-orders-for-reactivation` select requires `status='cancelled' AND completed_at IS NOT NULL AND completed_at > now() - interval '1 day'`. An order cancelled by the reservation clock fails that predicate, so it is never considered, the payment check is never run (`getDomainOrderPaymentStatus` in `apps/web/lib/billing/providers/autumn/client.ts` would have reported the balance as sufficient), and neither the reactivation branch nor the `refundUnfulfillableDomainOrder({ reason: 'reservation_expired' })` branch is reachable.
* Recovery lane 2 is the cancelled-order branch of `confirmDomainPurchase` in `apps/web/trpc/routers/billing.ts` (\~2614-2729), reached from the checkout return handler when the browser comes back with the checkout reference. It verifies account balances and, with the reservations gone, would mark the order refunded and cancel its add-on subscriptions. Production and provider state show it never completed for the reported order - the row's last write is the cancellation itself and the add-ons are still active and unconsumed - and why was not investigated. The fix should cover both lanes.
* `apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/billing/cleanup-stale-orders-cron.ts` documents the intended behaviour in its header comment: orders are cancelled on timeout because "the reconciliation cron ... will reactivate cancelled orders if the user pays within 24 hours of cancellation, so even if an order is cancelled, the user's payment won't be lost."

Because the payment flow can outlive the reservation window (a declined card retried a minute later is enough), the customer ends up with captured money, live add-on entitlements for domains and inboxes, a cancelled order, and zero provisioned records.

## Blast radius

Confirmed affected: 1 workspace, 1 user - a captured charge and zero provisioned domains/inboxes for that order (dashboard and inbox counts agree).

Potentially exposed: 125 pre-warmed orders across 94 distinct organizations in the state the recovery query rejects (the population is defined by the cancellation path, and most of it cancels within minutes of creating the order, i.e. through the manual cancel rather than the timer) - `status='cancelled' AND completed_at IS NULL AND order_type='pre_warmed' AND billing_account_id IS NOT NULL AND error='User cancelled the reservation'` - created 2026-06-26 to 2026-09-23; all 125 have zero associated mail-domain and mail-inbox rows. Counted 2026-09-24 with `select count(*), count(distinct organization_id) from domain_purchase_order where status='cancelled' and completed_at is null and order_type='pre_warmed' and billing_account_id is not null and created_at > now() - interval '90 days'`; the same predicate grouped by `error` returns that single error string for all 125.

Limitation and what blocks the exact figure: per-order payment state lives with the billing provider and is not mirrored in production data, so the pool cannot be split into charged-versus-simply-abandoned in bulk. The pool is the tightest reachable bound for exposure; the mechanism is deterministic, so any order in it whose payment lands after the cancellation lands in the same terminal state.

## Proposed fix

Make the cancelled-order payment-reactivation lane cover orders cancelled by the reservation clock: either record the terminal timestamp on that cancellation so the existing reactivation query sees the order, or widen the query to include cancelled pre-warmed orders with a NULL `completed_at` inside the reactivation window. Either way a payment that lands after cancellation must end in provisioning, or in a refund when the reservations are no longer held. Separately, the checkout timer should not cancel a reservation once a payment is in flight.

## What's included

In scope: the cancelled-order reactivation predicate and the cancellation write that feeds it, plus the checkout timer's interaction with a payment in progress.

Also worth filing separately, since each can ship and be owned on its own (not filed by this handoff):

* Containment: stop further customers from being charged into this state while the fix is pending.
* Customer recovery: for each already-affected workspace, provision the paid items or refund the captured amount - a human decision, and re-provisioning needs released domain names re-reserved.
* Observability: there is currently no signal that distinguishes "cancelled and abandoned" from "cancelled but paid", which is why this failure is invisible until a customer reports it.

Not applicable: no provider-side (mail provider) change - no provider order is ever created for these orders, so the mail provisioning pipeline is not involved.

## Regression seam

Boundary: the cancelled-order payment-reactivation pass of the reconcile cron, entered with an order cancelled by the reservation-expiry path. Trigger: a pre-warmed order cancelled through `cancelDomainReservation` (reservation timer expiry or the manual Back button) whose Autumn domain/inbox balances cover its ordered quantities. Observable red before the fix: the order is not selected, no per-order payment-check step runs, and the order stays `cancelled` with no provisioning and no refund. Green after: the order is selected, its payment is confirmed, and it either proceeds to provisioning or ends in the documented refund path with reservations released.

## Done when

* A pre-warmed order cancelled by the reservation-expiry path whose payment later succeeds is reactivated and provisioned, or refunded when its reservations are gone.
* No order can end in `cancelled` with captured payment, live entitlements, and zero provisioned items with no lane able to recover it.
* A regression test proves the causal mechanism at the reconcile-cron reactivation seam named above.
* The blast-radius count is re-run after deployment and the remaining exposed population is reported.

## Reports

* ENG-14198 - paid pre-warmed checkout, nothing provisioned or refunded.

relatedSnapshot.title: Master: unpaid mailboxes from a refunded DFY order cannot be paid from the billing page
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

The billing page cannot take payment for mailboxes that the platform still bills the provider for. When a Done-For-You domain order is refunded because the provider failed to provision it, the mailboxes it created are still live and in use, the audit flags them unpaid and warns they will be cancelled on a dated deadline, and the resubscribe control that would settle them never renders. Customers see a warning they cannot act on, and the mailboxes are removed while they are willing to pay.

## Problem

An owner opens Settings -> Billing from the "Review billing" banner, expecting to pay for the mailboxes the banner names. The page shows no managed domains for that workspace, so there is no "Review and resubscribe" and no per-domain "Resubscribe", and no other surface opens the pay dialog. Support then tells the customer a payment failed, when the only inbox charge was refunded.

## Root cause

`apps/web/trpc/routers/outreach/email-accounts.ts` `listManagedDomains` inner-joins the domain's purchase order and filters `ne(domainPurchaseOrderTable.status, 'refunded')` (and `ne(mailDomainTable.status, 'suspended')`). A refunded order therefore removes its domain from the managed list even while an open unpaid audit finding exists for it. `apps/web/components/billing/email-accounts-domains-card.tsx` `EmailAccountsDomainsCard` returns its "No managed domains" empty state before rendering the "Review and resubscribe" and per-domain "Resubscribe" buttons, and those are the only entry points to the pay flow (`apps/web/trpc/routers/cmr-domain-charges.ts` `listUnpaid` already returns the domain for an owner or admin, regardless of order status). When the card does render for a workspace with other domains, the refunded domain is still hidden from the list, so its per-domain control is missing too.

## Blast radius

Counted 2026-10-05 against production. 4 organizations and 9 open `unpaid` findings belong to a refunded purchase order; 2 of those organizations have an empty managed list, where the control is unreachable (6 findings), and the other 2 keep 3 and 4 visible managed domains, where only the per-domain control is missing (3 findings). All 4 organizations have a sent unpaid reminder dated 2026-09-29, so all 4 face a 2026-10-06 cancellation date. Distinct affected users were not counted: the audit rows carry no user id.

```
WITH f AS (SELECT fa.organization_id FROM cmr_domain_audit_finding fa
  JOIN domain_purchase_order o ON o.id = fa.order_id
  WHERE fa.payment_state = 'unpaid' AND fa.resolved_at IS NULL
    AND fa.dismissed_at IS NULL AND o.status = 'refunded')
SELECT f.organization_id::text, count(*) AS open_findings,
  (SELECT count(*) FROM mail_domain md
     JOIN domain_purchase_order o2 ON o2.id = md.order_id
    WHERE md.organization_id = f.organization_id
      AND md.status <> 'suspended' AND o2.status <> 'refunded') AS visible_managed_domains,
  (SELECT min(r.created_at)::text FROM cmr_renewal_reminder r
    WHERE r.organization_id = f.organization_id
      AND r.kind = 'unpaid' AND r.status = 'sent') AS first_sent_reminder
FROM f GROUP BY f.organization_id
```

Confirmed affected: 2 organizations with the control unreachable. Potentially exposed: the further 2 organizations whose refunded domain is hidden from the list while their pay-all control is reachable.

## Proposed fix

Make the unpaid-mailbox notice actionable for every workspace that carries an open unpaid finding. A workspace whose DFY order was refunded but whose provider mailboxes are still live should be able to pay for them from the billing page: the pay control should be reachable from the unpaid findings themselves rather than only from the managed domain list, and a refunded order's domain should stay visible to the billing card while an open unpaid finding exists so its per-domain "Resubscribe" renders as well. The customer-facing outcome is that the banner's deadline can be met from the billing page, without an operator making a production or billing change by hand.

## What's included

Both variants found in the blast radius (empty card, and refunded domain hidden beside visible ones). Not included: the upstream provisioning failure that leaves mailboxes live after a refunded order (owned by the DFY provisioning family tracked under ENG-13213), and the wording of the reminder emails. Related umbrella work: ENG-13358, whose child ENG-14423 covers giving customers a clear date to act by. Separately filed work needed for the current cohort: an operator must make the affected mailboxes payable, or decide they are removed, before 2026-10-06.

## Regression seam

The billing page's managed-domain list and its pay control. Red before: for a workspace whose only mail domain belongs to a refunded order while an open unpaid finding exists, `listManagedDomains` returns nothing and the billing card renders its empty state with no pay control. Green after: the same workspace offers a working resubscribe path that charges for the live mailboxes and clears the finding.

## Done when

* An owner of a workspace whose DFY order was refunded but whose provider mailboxes are live can open Settings -> Billing and pay for those mailboxes from the page.
* A workspace that also has other managed domains shows the per-domain resubscribe control for the refunded domain while its unpaid finding is open.
* A regression test at the list/pay seam proves both cases red before and green after.

## Reports

* ENG-14710 (customer report, Company Four workspace; carries the full investigation document).

relatedSnapshot.title: Unpaid mailboxes stop automatically on their resubscribe date
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

When a workspace passes its resubscribe date without paying, its unpaid mailboxes stop without anyone clicking anything. Renewal is switched off with the supplier, so the mailboxes lapse when the month we have already paid the supplier for ends, and our billing for them stops. Customers who pay late, before that month ends, get everything back.

## Problem

* The reminder email and billing page now tell customers their mailboxes "will be cancelled on {date}" (ENG-14418), but nothing acts on that date. Unpaid mailboxes keep running and we keep paying the supplier.
* Today an admin has to click Cancel on each domain after a 14 day grace counted from the weekly audit, so in practice about 21 days after detection.
* That admin cancel stops the supplier immediately and cannot be undone, even for a customer who pays a day late. It does not update our billing or our records.
* On 28 Sep, 1,153 domains (about 2,860 mailboxes, 241 workspaces) were unpaid, and 931 of them still renew with the supplier.

## User experience

* On the resubscribe date, if still unpaid: campaigns stop sending from those mailboxes, renewal is switched off with the supplier, and the customer gets "Your mailboxes will be removed on {supplier month end}. Resubscribe before then to keep them."
* Paying before the supplier month ends restores everything: renewal back on, billing re-attached, mailboxes still warm, no new setup.
* When the supplier month ends: the mailboxes are removed and the customer gets "Your mailboxes were removed."
* A workspace that pays before the resubscribe date is never touched.

No email or screen names the supplier.

## What's included

* A daily job that finds workspaces past their resubscribe date, re-checks live that they are still unpaid, and runs the shared cancel routine from ENG-14252 with supplier renewal off.
* Pin the resubscribe date once it has been emailed, so the date the job acts on is always the date the customer was told.
* The reactivation window and restore path.
* The two emails.
* A dry-run mode, a kill switch and a per-run limit for the first weeks, plus an admin view of what each run did.

Not included: the reminder emails and date display, which live in ENG-14100.

## Blocked by

* ENG-14252, for the safe cancel routine and the supplier renewal on/off call.

## Done when

- [ ] A test workspace that doesn't pay is stopped on its resubscribe date, the supplier shows renewal off, and billing shows no future charge.
- [ ] Paying inside the reactivation window restores everything with no new setup.
- [ ] A workspace that paid the day before the date is not touched.
- [ ] The date the job acts on always matches the date in the customer's first reminder.
- [ ] The daily billing check shows no unpaid domain past its date with supplier renewal on.

## Implementation context

* Today the date is derived from reminder history (`firstSentAtCovering` against `stateSince`), so it can move if an unpaid episode resets. ENG-14418 flags this. Pin it before enforcement relies on it.
* Supplier renewal off (`POST /subscriptions/toggle-autorenewal`) must be verified in the supplier sandbox first: the paid month keeps running, and switching renewal back on restores the mailboxes.
* The existing admin audit cancel uses the immediate supplier cancel. Keep that for explicit admin use only.
